issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a tensor-network helper named create_zero_state(num_qubits) but the template repository defines a function named init_zero_state(num_qubits) instead. This name mismatch (missing expected function name in the template) is structural: students following the problem statement will look for create_zero_state to implement or call, but the template exposes init_zero_state, causing confusion and preventing direct use of the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state with the same signature (create_zero_state(num_qubits: int) -> list[NDArray[np.complex128]]) or add a thin wrapper create_zero_state that calls init_zero_state. This will align the template with the problem statement and the solution while preserving the intended exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution reference a function named `create_zero_state` for initializing an MPS zero state, but the template repository defines the corresponding (stub) function as `init_zero_state`. This naming mismatch can confuse students searching for the prescribed API and mapping the task description to the template implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function `init_zero_state` to `create_zero_state` in template_repository/tensor_networks.py so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier (or alternatively update the problem statement to reference `init_zero_state`).
